about: Poolean rulebook versions, newest last. Each applies to games on or after its from date (null: every game before the first change). Kept by scripts/rulebook.mjs; a from date can be corrected by hand if a change was made on a game day before play.

sections.title: Scoring
lines: Baskets inside the three-point line are worth 2 points.
Baskets beyond the three-point line are worth 3 points.
The three-point line sits at about 60% of the pool's length from the basket.

sections.title: Possession
lines: Possession alternates after each score.
The team that is scored upon receives possession.
The scoring team may not touch the ball after a basket is made.

sections.title: Boundaries
lines: Touching the concrete outside the pool while in possession puts the ball out of bounds.
A ball that hits the coping (the white strip along the top edge of the pool walls) and bounces back in is still in play.
A ball that goes out of the pool any other way, including off the hoop pole, is out of bounds.

sections.title: Checking the ball
lines: After a basket, the ball is checked before play resumes.
After the ball goes out of bounds, no check is needed, but the ball must touch the back wall of the pool before play resumes.

sections.title: Goaltending
lines: Goaltending is prohibited.
A shot on its downward path, or with a reasonable chance of going in, may not be interfered with.
If goaltending occurs, the basket is automatically awarded.

subs.title: Cuddle bear rule
lines: On-ball hugs are allowed.
Off-ball hugs are prohibited.
Applies to both offensive and defensive players.

subs.title: What counts as a hug
lines: Wrapping or placing arms or hands around another player in a way that restricts their movement.

subs.title: Off-ball contact
lines: Boxing out, applying reasonable pressure, and using arms to hold position are all allowed off-ball.
Grabbing and hugging are prohibited off-ball.
The other player must always have an avenue to move away. No holding, grabbing, or trapping.

subs.title: Prohibited contact
lines: Dunking or forcing another player underwater.
Any contact involving a player's head or neck.
Grabbing and forcefully yanking an opposing player's arm, leg, or other limb.

sections.title: Rough play
lines: Roughness is judged case by case.
Control and sportsmanship come first.
When play gets heated, physicality eases off immediately.

subs.title: Calling fouls
lines: Players call their own fouls, without abusing the privilege.
A designated ref or third team, if present, may make the call.

subs.title: Settling a violation
lines: The player calling it can explain what happened. Anyone with a clear view can weigh in.
Players closest with the clearest view get more weight than those far away.
A violation stands if a majority agree it happened.
No majority or unclear facts defaults to no violation, and play resumes.

subs.title: Free throws
lines: No free throws for regular shooting fouls.
Free throws come only from penalties named in these rules.

subs.title: Unnecessary roughness
lines: A prohibited-contact violation or other unnecessarily rough conduct is two free throws from the three-point line.

sections.title: Basket and rim safety
lines: Hanging on the rim is prohibited.

sections.title: Timeouts
lines: One timeout per team per game.
Timeouts may only be called between possessions.

sections.title: General principle
lines: These rules keep the game competitive, safe, and fun.
Common sense and good sportsmanship cover anything these rules don't.
